assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass defect
items.clue: How much lighter a nucleus is than its separated nucleons.

items.label: Activity
items.clue: The number of nuclei in a sample that decay per unit time.

items.label: Penetration
items.clue: How far a radiation travels through matter before it is stopped.

items.label: Strong nuclear force
items.clue: The short-range attraction that holds protons and neutrons together.

questions.stem: Carbon-12 (¹²₆C) and carbon-14 (¹⁴₆C) are isotopes of carbon. Which statement about these two nuclides is correct?

options.text: They contain the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
Both contain the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons.
Their atoms have different chemical properties, as their nuclei differ.
Their nuclei are identical, but their atoms have different numbers of electrons.

questions.explanation: Both have proton number Z = 6, which is what makes them carbon. Carbon-12 has 12 − 6 = 6 neutrons and carbon-14 has 14 − 6 = 8, so they differ only in neutron number.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the binding energy of a nucleus?

options.text: The energy released when the nucleus is separated completely into its nucleons.
The energy stored inside the nucleus, which it gives out when it later decays.
The minimum energy needed to pull the nucleus apart into separate nucleons.
The energy equivalent of the extra mass a nucleus has over its separate nucleons.

questions.explanation: Nucleons attract one another through the strong nuclear force, so energy must be supplied to pull them apart. The binding energy is this energy; it equals the mass defect multiplied by c².

questions.stem: Approximate binding energies per nucleon are: ²₁H 1.1 MeV; ⁴₂He 7.1 MeV; ²⁸₁₄Si 8.4 MeV; ⁵⁶₂₆Fe 8.8 MeV; ¹¹⁸₄₆Pd 8.5 MeV; ²³⁶₉₂U 7.6 MeV. Which of these processes would release energy?

options.text: Splitting one ⁵⁶₂₆Fe nucleus into two ²⁸₁₄Si nuclei
Joining two ¹¹⁸₄₆Pd nuclei into one ²³⁶₉₂U nucleus
Separating one ⁴₂He nucleus into its four free nucleons
Fusing two ²₁H nuclei to form one ⁴₂He nucleus

questions.explanation: Both deuterium nuclei move far up the binding energy curve: the total binding energy rises from 2 × 2 × 1.1 = 4.4 MeV to 4 × 7.1 = 28.4 MeV, so about 24 MeV is released.

questions.stem: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?

options.text: ⁴⁰₁₈Ar and ⁴⁰₁₉K
³¹₁₅P and ³²₁₆S
²³₁₁Na and ²³₁₁Na⁺
³⁵₁₇Cl and ³⁷₁₇Cl

questions.explanation: Both nuclides have proton number Z = 17, so both are chlorine. They differ in nucleon number (35 and 37), so chlorine-35 has 18 neutrons and chlorine-37 has 20: the same element, different numbers of neutrons, which is what isotopes are.

questions.stem: The masses of a proton, a neutron and a helium-4 nucleus (⁴₂He) are 938.27 MeV c⁻², 939.57 MeV c⁻² and 3727.38 MeV c⁻² respectively. What is the binding energy per nucleon of helium-4?
questions.explanation: With masses in MeV c⁻², the mass defect in MeV c⁻² equals the binding energy in MeV: 2(938.27) + 2(939.57) − 3727.38 = 28.30 MeV. Dividing by the 4 nucleons gives 7.075 MeV per nucleon.

questions.stem: In the fusion reaction ²₁H + ³₁H → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n, the binding energies per nucleon are 1.11 MeV for ²₁H, 2.83 MeV for ³₁H and 7.07 MeV for ⁴₂He. A free neutron has no binding energy. How much energy is released in one reaction?

options.text: 10.7 MeV
17.6 MeV
28.3 MeV
3.13 MeV

questions.explanation: The energy released is the increase in total binding energy: 4(7.07) − [2(1.11) + 3(2.83)] = 28.28 − 10.71 = 17.6 MeV.

questions.stem: Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf − Φ.

questions.explanation: In the wave theory, energy spreads over the wavefront, so in dim light an electron would need time to absorb enough energy to escape. Experiment shows emission begins at once, because a single photon delivers all the energy one electron needs.

questions.stem: Which statement defines the threshold frequency of a metal?

options.text: The maximum frequency of light that can release photoelectrons from the metal
The frequency of light that releases the most photoelectrons per second from the metal
The frequency below which photoelectrons leave the metal only after a long delay
The lowest frequency of light that can release photoelectrons from the metal

questions.explanation: Below the threshold frequency f₀, each photon has less energy than the work function (hf < Φ), so no electron can be released, whatever the intensity. At f₀, hf₀ = Φ.

questions.stem: Ultraviolet radiation of wavelength 200 nm falls on a clean zinc plate. The work function of zinc is 4.30 eV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. What is the stopping potential for the photoelectrons?

In an electron diffraction tube the accelerating potential difference is 3.0 kV and one of the rings on the screen has a radius of 24 mm. The accelerating potential difference is increased to 6.0 kV. Assume the electrons are non-relativistic and that the radius of the ring is proportional to the de Broglie wavelength of the electrons. What is the new radius of this ring?

options.text: 12 mm
34 mm
24 mm
17 mm

questions.explanation: E_k = eV and p = √(2m_e eV), so λ = h/p ∝ 1/√V. Doubling V divides λ, and so the radius, by √2: 24 mm/√2 = 17 mm.

questions.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?

In Compton's experiment, X-rays of a single known wavelength were scattered by electrons in a block of graphite, and the wavelengths of the scattered X-rays were measured at several angles. Which result is evidence for the particle nature of light?

options.text: The scattered X-rays included a longer wavelength, shifted by an amount that increased with angle.
The scattered X-rays all had the same wavelength as the incident X-rays, at every angle.
X-rays were scattered in all directions, as balls would be when they hit a target.
The scattered X-rays included a longer wavelength, shifted in proportion to the incident wavelength.
